title: pg_trgm's picksplit applies GETSIGN() to a field that is already a bit vector, shifting the read TRGMHDRSIZE bytes past the signature
live_proof: upstream 1af08af694, "Fix pg_trgm's picksplit function with all-true datums" (CVE-2026-14678), backpatched through 14 and therefore absent at the 17.5 pin. The pin's own code proves the type error against itself. contrib/pg_trgm/trgm_gist.c:745 declares the field as `BITVECP sign;` -- a raw bit vector with no varlena header. :824 allocates `cache_sign = palloc(siglen * (maxoff + 1))` and :827 hands each entry the slice `&cache_sign[siglen * k]`, so every sign is exactly siglen bytes. :904 and :917 pass `cache[j].sign` DIRECTLY to hemdistsign as a BITVECP, which is the correct use. But :900 and :913 wrap the same field as `GETSIGN(cache[j].sign)`, and trgm.h:106 defines `GETSIGN(x)` as `( (BITVECP)( (char*)x+TRGMHDRSIZE ) )` with TRGMHDRSIZE = VARHDRSZ + sizeof(uint8) at trgm.h:74. The pointer is therefore advanced past a header the object does not have, and sizebitvec then reads siglen bytes from there -- running TRGMHDRSIZE bytes off the end of that entry's slice, and off the end of the whole palloc'd cache_sign buffer when j is the last entry. As upstream notes, the cast inside GETSIGN is what stops the compiler warning.
fidelity: real server, real allocator, contrib extension. The read is of a palloc'd chunk, so whether a mechanism sees it depends on whether TRGMHDRSIZE bytes is enough to leave the surrounding aset block -- it is a small overread, so the expectation is that it is not, which is exactly the asymmetry this corpus measures. Trigger verified on a native 17.5 cluster on 2026-10-06: the first version used rows long enough that CREATE INDEX failed with "index row requires 10464 bytes, maximum size is 8191" before picksplit ran at all -- the defect was unreachable and the case would have taken a VM slot to prove nothing. At 60 md5-chunks per row and 6000 rows the index builds to about 3700 pages, so gtrgm_picksplit runs repeatedly over a mixture of all-true and sparse signatures, which is the branch condition. The server completes normally and answers queries, as expected: the overread is TRGMHDRSIZE = VARHDRSZ + 1 bytes inside a palloc'd slice, which no unmodified build can see. Reaching it is what the trigger has to guarantee; reporting it is the arms' job.

status: measured on virtual Capstone (virtual-malloc, virtual-pg-pools) and stock CheriBSD (cheribsd-revocation); each arm's verdict_from names its bundle. The physical spatial/sublet pair measured 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-10 stays in results/
nested_why: The object is a palloc chunk, which AllocSet carves out of a block it took from malloc, so the defect is nested by the allocator that served it.
note: Re-measured 2026-10-21 with fault_sites ABSENT, which is what settles this cell. The list was ["gtrgm_picksplit", "pg_popcount_optimized"] and its own fault_sites_why began "Derived from the source, not from a run". shared/run-arm.py:355 runs control.sql only `if o.fault and o.reached and not o.attribution`, so while the list stood the declared site matched the pc first and the paired control never ran: the CAUGHT rested on a hand-written list rather than on a measurement. With the list gone the fault is unattributed by site, the runner falls through to control.sql, and the control -- the same GiST trigram index build over sparse rows only, so no signature goes all-true and the defective branch is never entered -- COMPLETED on this image. The verdict is unchanged and is now a measurement: cause=28 in pg_popcount_optimized, attributed by control. The source chain the list was read off is confirmed rather than contradicted -- the fault lands in exactly the symbol the chain predicts, and the pc differs from the 2026-10-18 run only in load base (0x3f92b39538 against 0x3fbcb39538) -- so the declaration was correct; it was simply doing a job that a control should do. No other cell moved: all nine verdicts are identical to results/2026-10-18-review, and 07 is the only case whose attribution route changed (function -> control).
